page.content:
The Roman Empire in the east — Constantinople, Orthodox rite, and a thousand years after Rome in the west fell.

How Byzantine Empire connects

  • Location: Constantinople — Constantinople was the imperial capital.
  • Event: Fall of Constantinople — The 1453 fall ended the Byzantine state.
  • Character: Justinian I — Justinian I ruled the sixth-century empire at its reconquest peak.
  • Character: Constantine XI Palaiologos — Constantine XI was the last Byzantine emperor.
  • Character: Heraclius — Heraclius ruled through the last Persian war and the first Arab conquests.
  • Character: Basil II — Basil II brought the Macedonian-era empire to a territorial high.
  • Character: Alexios I Komnenos — Alexios I restored the state after Manzikert and met the First Crusade.
  • Location: Hagia Sophia — Hagia Sophia is the empire's emblematic church.
  • Concept: Theme system — Themes were the middle-period military geography of the empire.

What is Byzantine Empire?

The Byzantine Empire is the eastern Roman state that ruled from Constantinople after the west fragmented. Its lore runs through Justinian and Theodora, Hagia Sophia, Greek fire, the theme system, the Komnenoi, the Fourth Crusade, and the 1453 fall to the Ottomans.

Key threads lead to Constantinople, Fall of Constantinople, Justinian I, Constantine XI Palaiologos, Heraclius and Basil II.
